claim: Removing Brahui from the set of attested Dravidian languages and reporting the geographic measurement on the remaining languages shows something about where Dravidian was spoken - that the family's centre of gravity is southern and eastern and that Brahui's northwestern position is therefore anomalous and in need of a migration explanation.

notes: SUPERSEDED BY DMB-002. This row is the interpretation the owner challenged, written out in full so that it is not re-proposed. It is retained under the CLAUDE.md standing constraint that correction history is preserved and rejected reasoning stays visible. It is NOT deleted. Two distinct defects: (a) it reads a delete-one sensitivity statistic as a substantive claim about a language family's geography (BF-005); (b) it treats the twenty-odd attested Dravidian languages as independent points, which they are not if any of them subgroup (BF-006). claim: A leave-one-out distance statistic over attested Dravidian language locations measures how much of that statistic's value rests on a single language. Deleting Brahui and recomputing the distance from a northwestern reference to the nearest remaining language supports a statement about the instrument's exposure to one datapoint, and about the size of the gap between Brahui and the next-nearest attested Dravidian language. It does not support any statement about where Dravidian was spoken at any date: the statistic has no chronological term, the attested set is a survival sample rather than a sample of past distribution, and the reference point is a free parameter of the analyst's choosing.

claim: OWNER OBJECTION 2, as raised: the measurement is Euclidean distance to a northwestern reference and cannot see subgroup structure. Brahui, Kurukh and Malto are conventionally North Dravidian; if that grouping holds, Brahui's position is supported by shared descent rather than standing alone.
notes: Recorded as RAISED BY THE OWNER. Two separable propositions, which unit 2 keeps apart: (a) a distance-to-reference statistic contains no term for shared descent and so cannot represent a clade - this is a property of the statistic; (b) Brahui, Kurukh and Malto form a clade - this is a claim about Dravidian, and it is the one the owner explicitly instructed must be measured rather than asserted. (a) is addressed at DMB-014; (b) at DMB-017 to DMB-022, and its contested status at DMB-023 to DMB-026. Logged as method failure BF-006.

claim: This measurement sits inside the scope of constitution section 4.M, Brahui, Kurukh and Malto, which requires six competing models to be held open: long-term northwestern survival; later long-distance migration; broader ancient distribution followed by language replacement; continuing dialect networks followed by fragmentation; small migrating group plus extensive local language adoption; and complex combinations. Treating Brahui as detachable from the Dravidian set - as a datapoint whose removal leaves the rest of the family intact and interpretable - presupposes the second or the fifth of those models, in which Brahui arrives from elsewhere and is therefore separable from a family whose real distribution lies elsewhere. Under the first, third and fourth models Brahui is not detachable, because on those models it is not an addition to the distribution but a survival of it.
